prompt_text:
The figure summarizes several fabrication routes for building low-dimensional (LD) perovskite layers on top of 3D perovskite films, and then integrating them into LD/3D heterostructures. Overall, it contrasts wet-solution and dry-processing strategies and shows how these methods can create a thin LD surface layer, a bottom LD/3D structure, or an interlayer between the two phases.

In the upper part, LD perovskites are first formed either by coating and annealing a precursor solution, by directional in-plane solid-phase growth, or by dry evaporation and hybrid two-step methods involving PbI2 and LD ligands. These schemes emphasize solvent removal, annealing, and film stacking as the key steps that define LD growth.

The middle part focuses on bottom-structure formation. One route forms LD material in situ by mixing hole-transport and ligand components or by adding ligand and 3D perovskite “ink” together, while another route builds the LD and 3D layers sequentially, for example by depositing an LD film first and then adding the 3D perovskite on top.

The bottom part highlights interlayers placed between LD and 3D regions, including crosslinked polymers, metal oxides such as Al2O3 and VOx, and 2D carbon materials like graphene oxide and reduced graphene oxide.
